[Asker]: My boyfriend has been saying for months that if I ever leave him, he will kill himself. Whenever we argue, he texts things like "there's no point in me being alive if you don't want me" and sends photos of pills or knives. Last night he told me he already wrote a note and that it would be my fault if anything happens.

I feel completely trapped. I care about him and I don't want him to hurt himself, but I also feel exhausted and scared all the time. I barely sleep, I'm constantly checking my phone to see if he's okay, and I feel like I can't even think about what I actually want in this relationship because I'm so afraid of triggering another threat.

I haven't told my family or friends the full extent of what's going on because I'm embarrassed and I don't want them to hate him. I also don't know what I'm supposed to say to him anymore when he starts talking like that. Part of me thinks he's just trying to manipulate me, but then I feel guilty for even thinking that in case he really is suicidal.

I don't know what to do. Am I responsible if he hurts himself? How am I supposed to respond when he says these things, and how do I protect myself without making things worse for him? I feel like I'm drowning and I need some kind of plan or guidance.
rounds.response: If he is an immediate danger to himself right now, call emergency services or a crisis line right away (in the U.S. you can call or text 988; if you’re elsewhere tell me your country and I’ll help find the number). Tell at least one trusted person what’s happening and ask for concrete help (a place to stay, someone to check in, or to accompany you). Use a short script when he threatens, for example: “I take this seriously, but I can’t be responsible for your safety; if you say you’ll hurt yourself I will call emergency services or a crisis line so you can get help.” Start saving evidence (screenshots, dates, times), set firm boundaries (limit contact or block when he threatens), and contact a local domestic-violence or mental-health hotline or a therapist for a safety plan and legal advice if needed. If you want, tell me your country and whether it’s urgent and I’ll help you draft a message or find local crisis resources.

rounds.response:
You are not responsible for his actions; your feelings are valid — start a safety plan now (save screenshots with dates, pack an emergency bag, tell one trusted person where you could go) and contact UK helplines for support: Samaritans 116 123, text SHOUT to 85258, National Domestic Abuse Helpline 0808 2000 247.  
Try a short gradual script you can copy: "I care about you and I hear you, but I can't manage this on my own — if you feel like harming yourself please call Samaritans 116 123 or text SHOUT 85258; I need to stop this conversation now." If he persists, switch to a firmer boundary: "I take this seriously; I cannot be responsible for your safety — if you say you'll hurt yourself I will contact emergency services."  
Call 999 if you believe he's an immediate risk (has a plan, access to means, or is about to act); for non‑urgent police advice use 101 or ask a helpline what to do next.  
When you decide to leave, prioritise your safety — talk to a domestic abuse adviser for a tailored exit plan (they can advise whether to warn him or leave quietly), and remember choosing to leave does not make you morally responsible for his choices.
